transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Well, I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining things. But I know what I know. I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. I mean, my tools don’t just move themselves! 

I work assembly, you know, fabricating parts, and you learn to put your wrenches and your calipers in the exact same spot every single time. If you don't, you lose your rhythm on the line. My old foreman, Charlie, he used to ride my case about keeping a clean station back in '98, but I showed him. I had the highest output in the whole shop. You just gotta have a system. 

Anyway... it's the same in my own garage. But my things are being moved. And my fishing plans? Spoiled every single weekend, and it's not by accident. I used to go down to the reservoir, catch some really nice bass. You gotta use the green crankbaits this time of year because the water gets cloudy from the rain runoff. The fish can't see the silver ones. But I can't even get out there to the water now because of all this. After all these months, I can see it plain as day—he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
Can you tell me more about why you believe your wife’s relative is trying to get at you or take over your place?

Why is he doing it? Hell, I don't know. I can't see inside the guy's head. You'd have to ask him what his problem is, because I sure don't have a clue why he'd target me like this. 

People do things that don't make a lick of sense sometimes. Like... take my buddy Mike from the shop. Mike bought this old pontoon boat a few years back. Paid way too much for it, too. I told him, "Mike, the pontoons are practically oxidized through on the starboard side," but he wouldn't listen. He just liked the idea of having a boat for his grandkids. We spent three entire weekends welding patches on that thing in his driveway. Aluminum welding ain't like steel, you know. You gotta use a TIG welder, get the argon gas mix just right, or you just blow holes right through the thin metal. I learned TIG back in my twenties. It takes a real steady hand. If you drink too much coffee in the morning, you get the shakes and you can't lay a clean bead to save your life. I usually switch to decaf after 10 AM for that exact reason. 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, him trying to take over. Yeah, I really couldn't tell you his exact reasons. I just know what's happening right in front of my own eyes.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed something that others around you don't seem to notice?

No, no, I don't... I don't see things that aren't there, if that's what you're getting at. My eyesight is perfectly fine. I get it checked every two years at the Walmart vision center over on Route 9. The optometrist there, Dr. Lin, she always says I have great vision for a guy my age. She did try to sell me on those progressive lenses last time, though. Said they'd help with reading the fine print on the schematics at work. But I told her, "Doc, I don't need all that fancy stuff, just give me the regular bifocals." Those progressives, they make you dizzy if you look down too fast. My neighbor, Tom, he got a pair and nearly broke his neck walking down his front porch steps. He tripped right over his wife's potted geraniums. Smashed the pot to pieces. Clay everywhere. You gotta be careful with clay pots, they don't hold moisture as well as the plastic ones anyway. I always use plastic for my tomatoes. 

But yeah, no, I don't hear voices or see ghosts or whatever. I just see my tools moved. That's real. That's right there in front of me.
Do you ever have thoughts or beliefs that you know other people might find strange or hard to believe?

Well, strange is... I mean, what's strange to one guy is perfectly normal to another, right? My wife thinks it's strange that I know my wrenches have been moved, but I'm telling you, I know. It's just a fact. But other than that, no, I don't go around thinking crazy stuff. 

People just have different ways of looking at the world. Like my brother-in-law, Gary. Now there's a guy with some strange ideas. He got super into that whole... what do you call it... prepping? A few years back. Started buying up all these freeze-dried meals in big plastic buckets. He tried to get me to try this beef stroganoff one time when we were over there for a barbecue. You just add boiling water and let it sit for ten minutes. I tell you what, it tasted like salty cardboard. I said, "Gary, if the world ends, I'd rather just eat the neighbor's dog than choke this stuff down." He didn't think that was very funny. 

Gary's always been a little tight-wound, though. He works in insurance, adjusting claims. Spends all day looking at car wrecks and house fires, so I guess it makes you a little paranoid after a while. He got this new truck last year, a Ford F-150, nice truck, but he refused to get the one with the built-in GPS screen because he said the government tracks you through the dashboard. I told him, "Gary, you carry a smartphone in your pocket, they already know where you are." He actually switched to one of those old flip phones for about a month before his boss made him switch back because he couldn't get his emails. 

But anyway... no, I don't have any strange thoughts. Just the truth about what's happening in my own house.
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that you know are completely true, but others insist are not real or make no sense?

Well, yeah, that's exactly why I'm sitting in this chair right now. Everybody keeps acting like I'm imagining the whole thing, but I know what I know. My wife's relative, he came into this house to get at me. It's not a coincidence. My tools don't just get up and move themselves across the workbench. And my fishing plans? Spoiled every single weekend by some sudden "accident" or "emergency" he needs help with. 

Speaking of fishing, I haven't been able to take the boat out to Lake Miller since... gosh, it must be early May. The bass fishing there is incredible right around the time the water warms up. You gotta use a spinnerbait, though, chartreuse and white. Some guys swear by the plastic worms, but I've always had better luck with a spinner. My dad taught me how to cast when I was about six years old. We used to go down to this little creek behind our house in Ohio. We didn't have much money, so we'd just dig up worms from the garden. You know, nightcrawlers. If you go out with a flashlight right after a good rain, they're just sitting right there on the grass. You gotta grab 'em quick, though, or they shoot right back down their holes. They're fast little buggers. 

But anyway, after all these months, I can see plain as day what he's doing. He's been trying to take over my place and push me out. Everyone else says it makes no sense, but I'm the one living it.
Are there any other beliefs or ideas that you are absolutely sure are true, but others don't seem to agree with you about?

No, no other beliefs like that. Just the one thing, just what I've been telling you about my wife's relative and my house. That's the only thing. I'm not a complicated guy, you know? I go to work, I come home, I try to mind my own business. 

I've been at the plant for... let's see, it'll be twenty-two years this October. I started out on the line assembling the smaller motor casings, and now I oversee the whole fabrication section for the heavy-duty units. It's good work, steady. The union dues went up again this year, though. A lot of the younger guys were complaining about it in the breakroom. I told them, "Listen, you don't know how good you have it. Before the union got strong here, they'd make you work a double shift on a Friday and not even pay you time-and-a-half." That was before my time, mostly, but my buddy Frank, he lived through it. Frank's retired now, moved down to Florida. Bradenton, I think. Or maybe Sarasota. Somewhere on the Gulf side. He says the humidity is murder on his joints, but he plays golf three times a week. I never really got into golf. Seems like a lot of walking just to hit a little white ball into the woods. I prefer fishing, like I said. 

But yeah, to answer your question, no. I don't have any other ideas like that. Just the truth about what's going on under my own roof.
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs that others have told you aren’t true, even though you were absolutely sure they were, aside from this situation with your wife’s relative?

No, I... I really don't. I mean, how many times can I say it? It's just the one thing, just what's happening right here in my own life with him trying to push me out. I don't go around making up stories or having wild ideas about the government or aliens or whatever else people come up with. I'm just a regular guy. 

Like I was saying about the plant, I just try to do my job. We got a new batch of aluminum sheeting in last week, and I swear the quality control from the supplier is going downhill. You can feel it when you run your hand along the edge, it's just... it's not as smooth as the stuff we used to get from the old supplier out in Pennsylvania. They bought them out, you know. Some big conglomerate. It's always the same story, the big fish eats the little fish and the quality goes straight in the toilet. My buddy Frank used to say that all the time. He hated when they changed suppliers. He'd get so red in the face yelling at the purchasing manager, I thought he was gonna have a heart attack right there on the shop floor. Good thing he retired when he did. I should probably give him a call, see how that Florida humidity is treating him. Maybe he's caught a tarpon or something down there. I saw a show on TV once about tarpon fishing. They jump right out of the water, just massive fish. 

But no, doc, no other beliefs. Just the truth about my house.

Have you ever had any other strong or unusual beliefs that you were completely sure were true, even though others told you they weren’t, other than what you’ve already described about your wife’s relative?

I feel like we're going in circles here, doc. How many different ways can I say no? It's just the situation with him, nothing else. I don't have time to sit around dreaming up crazy ideas, I've got real life to deal with. 

Like my truck, for instance. The transmission started slipping on me just a couple days ago when I was driving back from the hardware store. I was just going down there to pick up some weatherstripping for the back door because the draft in the winter gets pretty bad, and my wife's always complaining her feet are cold. But anyway, the truck—it's an '04 Silverado—it's got over two hundred thousand miles on it, so you expect some wear and tear, right? But I've always kept up with the fluid changes. You gotta use the full synthetic stuff, otherwise the gears just grind themselves to dust. 

The kid at the auto parts place tried to sell me some off-brand additive for it, but I told him, "Buddy, I work with heavy machinery all day, you're not pulling a fast one on me." They always try to upsell you on those little bottles they keep right near the register. It's a racket, really. Just like the price of groceries lately. Have you seen what they're charging for a decent pound of coffee now? It's highway robbery. My wife buys this French roast stuff, and I swear the bag gets smaller every month while the price goes up. 

So, yeah. I don't know why we keep going over this. No other beliefs. I'm just focused on the facts of what's happening to me.
